title: Commodity intelligence and its engineered environment
claim: *Commodity intelligence and its engineered environment.* Training develops general-purpose capabilities; the harness turns reasoning into action. The engineer maintains the system knowledge and mechanisms that guide the agent, constrain its actions, and evaluate whether selected results may be accepted. Training data need not all be public.
purpose: Distinguish capability acquisition from agent operation and identify the engineer's principal locus of control.

topology.description: Three vertically connected regions: model development, an acting agent composed of deployed foundation model and harness, and the engineered environment containing the existing system and engineering structure. Training stages connect left to right; trained weights enter the deployed foundation model. Agent actions change the existing system; guidance and governance flow back to agentic work. An external engineer principally maintains the environment and can optionally affect training or fine-tuning.

relations.solid: Directed causation, action, guidance, governance or engineering maintenance as explicitly labeled.
relations.dashed: Optional model training or fine-tuning, when available.

alt: Training data leads through pretraining and post-training to trained foundation-model weights. A deployed foundation model and agentic harness form the acting agent. The model's broad semantic reasoning enables delegated implementation; probabilistic output calls for independent assurance; bounded working state calls for external representations; inexpensive repeated reasoning calls for scalable governance. The agent changes an existing system comprising code, architecture, documentation, configuration, tests and operational state. Engineering structures supply guidance and govern selected actions and results. The engineer principally engineers and maintains this environment; training or fine-tuning is an optional connection.
bw_encoding: 5% black fill identifies the model-development and environment regions; the heavier environment border identifies the engineer's principal sphere of control. Components and ordinary nodes are white. Text is black. Only the optional training relation is dashed and lightened.
typography: Bundled Source Sans 3; 11.5 pt region headings, 10.8 pt component headings, 10–10.5 pt ordinary labels, 9.5 pt relation and column annotations. Bold names regions/components; italic annotations distinguish the property/implication column roles and the system being changed. No shrink-to-fit.
routing: Orthogonal connectors only. The training-to-deployment route enters a clear left port of the foundation-model panel. Guidance and governance use separate upward ports; actions use a downward port. The optional training route runs outside all panels on the right, with a vertical relation label beside the shaft. Rotation keeps the full qualification legible without consuming the region width.
redesign: Replaces the old parallel lists/converging-agent figure with the author's model-origin, agent-operation and environmental-control distinction. Adds all four property/implication mappings and the existing system as an explicit object of change.

web_counterpart.inspection: Rendered web counterpart contains the same text, boxes, ports and directed/optional relations. A fallback-font rendering was also inspected for fit.
web_counterpart.audit_note: SVG heuristic reports one canvas-overflow candidate for the rotated optional-training label because it measures it as horizontal. Native PDF geometry reports no overflow or collision; the rotated SVG was inspected.
